newsitem.title: CHINA: China punishes listed firm for trading own shares.
newsitem.headline: China punishes listed firm for trading own shares.

text.p: China's top securities watchdog has fined a Shenzhen-listed A share firm for illegally trading its own shares, the Shanghai Securities News said on Saturday.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) fined Zhangjiajie Tourism Development Co Ltd two million yuan, the newspaper said.
The firm's chairman, general manager and deputy general manager were fined 50,000 yuan each, it said.
China's Company Law and securities trading rules ban listed firms from trading their own shares.

The CSRC had also ruled that the Hunan Securities Trading Centre had violated the rules by allowing Zhangjiajie to illegal trade its own shares, and had fined the centre 750,000 yuan, the newspaper said.
The newspaper said a CSRC investigation had found that Zhangjiajie had illegally bought more than two million of its own shares with 41.5 million yuan from September 2 to November 18 last year.
On November 18, 20 and 21, the company sold 1.432 million shares before it announced a bonus issue on November 22, making a profit of 11.805 million yuan, it said.
"The transactions violated the Company Law and securities rules," the newspaper quoted the CSRC as saying in a circular.
"The company's act of buying its own shares and then selling them just prior to a bonus issue was also an instance of insider trading," the circular said.
The CSRC decided to confiscate Zhangjiajie's profits from the illegal trades and ordered the firm to sell the shares it still held within two months, the newspaper said.

The watchdog also ordered the company to quickly convene a shareholdings' meeting to discuss the dismissal of general manager Yang Zhezhong and deputy general manager Li Jianzhang, who are responsible for the illegal trading, it said.
